listing.name: Might and Magic VII (OpenEnroth)
listing.summary: Research listing. Upstream route: Official README says MM7 playable; desktop nightly packages available. Limits: MM7 playable upstream; MM6/MM8 planned. Nightly-only releases may contain bugs. Upstream platforms: Nightly Windows x86/x86-64 ZIPs, Linux x86-64 Flatpak, macOS ARM64/x86-64 DMGs and Android universal APK. MM7 current; other MM games remain planned. Original data: Supply original Might and Magic VII game data, from a GOG installation or another installed/extracted retail copy: at least ANIMS, DATA, MUSIC and SOUNDS directories. Point OPENENROTH_MM7_PATH at that data when needed. MM6/MM8 are planned targets, not substitutes for MM7 assets; exact accepted language/patch revision is not pinned in retained README. Portcove setup/gameplay not verified.

steps.title: Use a complete compatible Might and Magic VII copy
steps.instruction: Prepare OpenEnroth upstream using your own supported Might and Magic VII installation and its ANIMS, DATA, MUSIC and SOUNDS trees. Planned Might and Magic VI/VIII support does not make their data interchangeable. Choose the actual compatible Windows CPU/build variant and native OpenEnroth.exe, retaining its libraries and resources. A moving nightly name does not establish compatibility with an arbitrary copy.

steps.title: Retain the separate data and user coordinates
steps.instruction: Keep the actual working directory and established literal --data-path and --user-path arguments. --portable defaults both paths to the working directory; an existing .portable file can also select portable mode. Do not add either merely to register. Existing OPENENROTH_MM7_PATH and upstream automatic discovery can affect data selection; Portcove does not inject that environment. Windows normally uses Saved Games/OpenEnroth for user state, with a working-directory fallback when the known-folder lookup is unavailable. Preserve the actual selected paths and openenroth.ini.

steps.title: Preserve both sides of upstream save copying
steps.instruction: When the data and user roots differ and the destination saves directory is empty, startup can copy regular files from the data saves directory into the user saves directory. It leaves the originals in place and skips copying into a nonempty destination. Keep both complete trees, all configuration, saves, modifications and unknown files before running a changed build. This upstream copying does not establish backward-save compatibility or a Portcove migration.

steps.title: Check the working copy before registration
steps.instruction: Finish upstream setup and a normal start/quit using the intended copy before attaching it. Retain its exact native executable, working directory and established supported literal arguments. Review the selected intent and consent, then choose Play separately. Attaching a copy does not certify the game, its original assets or its save compatibility.

steps.title: Keep updates and removal under the existing owner
steps.instruction: Close all actual game instances before changing files. Keep the old creating runtime and every actual data/profile root recoverable, make deliberate compatible updates upstream, then review/relink a changed executable before the next Play. Upstream/player owns preparation, updates, writes, migration and recovery. Portcove supervises its selected process; this is not an exclusive instance lock or a sandbox. Removing this registration preserves external files. This route does not offer Portcove-managed downloads, setup, updates, backup, rollback, migration or external-file deletion.

warnings: Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant rights to original game assets, music, mods or bundled components.
Preserve every actual external runtime and player-data location before upstream changes. Shared profiles are not isolated by choosing a different executable.
